tasks.description: Give `/audit-design --drift` its own rubric: the `driftRubric` input in `audit-design.js`, a stated mapping from comparison verdicts to findings, a reported finding when `driftRubric` is missing, and the `/audit-design` command text that passes it.
Name the to-be board's id in `create-design.js`'s screen-critic prompt, and filter `scoreFindings` to the to-be board(s) the critic was given.
In `design-map.js` `direction()`, don't report `style_pack` blank when `style` is given, and read a decimal touch-target floor.

Make the corpus replay survive a failed critic run without hiding it, keep a missing or unstartable critic CLI fatal, and confine label paths to the corpus folder; add tests for all three to `replay.test.js`.
Read the targets' rectangles once in the overlap measure, and restore the missing ` * ` on the render CLI's doc-comment line.

could_not_verify: That the drift comparison judges better with its own rubric. That needs a live `/audit-design --drift` run; the unit test proves only which text reaches the prompt.
The overlap measure's speed-up is not measured; the claim rests on reading 500 rectangles once rather than about 250,000 times.
